liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Abrupt endings sound like a leader's hand signal in rehearsal rather than tape shut-offs [10]
- **Stealin'** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Stealin' as a reason to download the show [12]
- **You Don't Love Me** (1 review): Reviewer finds this version awesome and says the Allmans later ran with the song [6]
- **Good Morning, Lil' School Girl** (1 review): Reviewer calls the extra version of this song outstanding [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **She's On The Road Again**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]
- **Hey Little One**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 7 archived performances [15]
- **Stealin'**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 14 archived performances [15]
- **Stealin'**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 14 archived performances [15]
- **You Don't Love Me**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 4 archived performances [15]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Next Time You See Me, Cold Rain & Snow, Good Morning, Lil' School Girl, Good Morning, Lil' School Girl [15]

## The recordings

- **gd66-02-25.sbd.unknown.1593.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 57 min; rated 4.77/5 by 52 [1]. Said about its sound: Excellent sound, with slight distortion on Jerry's vocal mic, attributed to a pushed ribbon mic rather than digital distortion; Hiss appears when this song starts, and the reviewer thinks the rest sounds like a different show; Recording quality is excellent for its age [4][5][12]
- **gd1966-02-25.sbd.unknown.20346.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 57 min; rated 4.24/5 by 17 [2]

## Around the show

- Date is only reported; the tape may be labeled ??/??/66, and a different shn set circulates under that label [1]
- DeadBase assigned 2/25 but noted the date of the list is uncertain [3]
- Reviewer says Pigpen and Phil are especially strong, and the band seems to be experimenting [6]
- Reviewer says Pigpen sings cleanly throughout and takes a solo, and Jerry plays superbly [8]
- Reviewer notes DeadBase 10 lacks a setlist for this date; the tape may be a studio rehearsal rather than a show [10]
- The Ivar Theater was at 1605 North Ivar Ave, Hollywood [11]
- Tom Waits's song 'Emotional Weather Report' mentions the Ivar Theater's ticket taker on a Saturday night [14]
- Reviewer says performance and soundboard quality differ sharply from the 1/8, 3/12 and 3/25 shows, doubting the early-year date [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd66-02-25.sbd.unknown.1593.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Transfer chain listed as master reel to DAT to CD, then shn [1]
- **gd1966-02-25.sbd.unknown.20346.sbeok.shnf**: source: MR>DATx>CD [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by gdlistening.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead at the (possibly) Ivar Theater - 2/25/66](https://gdlistening.blogspot.com/2011/10/grateful-dead-at-possibly-ivar-theater.html) [16]
